stories.title: Medical record interface study identifies usability flaws
stories.summary: A qualitative study of an electronic medical record interface in two intensive care units found that design flaws, including restricted user control and irreversible actions, accounted for fifty-seven percent of all recorded usability violations. The research was conducted at a large teaching hospital in Shiraz, southern Iran.

stories.title: Nigeria sees internet user growth
stories.summary: Nigeria reached 116 million internet users in October 2026, an increase of 7.1 million over the previous year, according to DataReportal. As the digital audience expands, companies face pressure to build products that are functional and intuitive. Artificial intelligence is now a focus for many local CEOs.

stories.title: How Without brought boutique hospitality to a £1bn corporate monolith - Design Week
Branding as a tool for recognition
stories.summary: Nonprofits and rural social enterprises often struggle to build distinct identities because their work remains known only to those directly involved. Branding is presented as the solution for helping audiences understand an organisation's purpose and approach, allowing others to learn from their experience and insights.

stories.title: The debate over designers coding in production
stories.summary: Design engineers are divided on whether designers should work directly from production codebases or maintain separate prototyping sandboxes. While some advocate for treating the production environment as the single source of truth, the effort required to maintain this workflow remains a significant practical hurdle for many teams.

stories.title: Studio Kiln rebrands weight-loss app Reset
stories.summary: Studio Kiln has redesigned the weight-loss app Reset, which uses a face scan and habit questionnaire to assign users to specific types. CEO Bryan Cartwright stated the previous branding felt dated and conventional. The app now features a guide named Ester to manage meal planning for users.

stories.title: Generative UI loaders released on GitHub
stories.summary: Generative Loaders, a set of React components for generative UI, has launched with over 218,000 installs. The library provides sixteen different animation styles, including typewriter, skeleton, and dissolve effects, designed for developers to implement during data loading states in applications.

stories.title: Automation and accessibility concerns
stories.summary: The rise of automated content generation presents specific challenges for disabled users who have limited capacity to manage the resulting volume of information. The author argues that even if underlying technical issues with generative AI were resolved, the impact of automated workflows remains a significant accessibility problem.

stories.title: Father studio uses hydrophones for coastal film
stories.summary: Creative studio Father produced a short film titled Can You Hear This? by recording Kent’s coastline with hydrophones and contact mics. The project follows the principle of showing rather than telling, aiming to let the sound of the environment communicate the brand's message to the audience.

stories.title: Yury Ostromentsky releases Backslanted typeface series
stories.summary: Designer Yury Ostromentsky has released Backslanted, a typeface series featuring inverted italics. The project was created in response to the designer's feeling of being overturned following the start of the war in Ukraine. The series experiments with various styles, weights, and angles across the font family.

stories.title: DixonBaxi updates EA Sports FC 27 identity
stories.summary: DixonBaxi has updated the EA Sports FC 27 brand identity by applying the existing triangle mark across various formats, including wireframes and pixelated edges. The studio aims to keep the shape consistent while changing its behavior. The brand now uses the tagline that FC is lived.

stories.title: Otherway redesigns The Whisky Exchange identity
stories.summary: Otherway has updated The Whisky Exchange brand identity, replacing traditional dark greens and browns with a vibrant purple palette. The studio redrew the company's twin-lion crest to appear lighter and more fluid, aiming to move the brand away from a ceremonial aesthetic toward something more accessible.

stories.title: Fix Studio designs identity for Puerto Rico IOC archive
stories.summary: Fix Studio has created a visual identity for the Instituto de Observación Colectiva, featuring an interlocking IOC monogram and concrete-poetry grids. The archive, founded in 2026 by Christopher Gregory-Rivera, supports photography focused on Puerto Rico and its diaspora through workshops, fellowships, and exhibitions.

stories.title: Alphamark creates split-screen design for Studio Plato
stories.summary: Alphamark has developed a website for Studio Plato that uses a locked, full-viewport split-screen diptych. The design displays two views of the same interior space within a single frame, with navigation elements floating over the photography. The site does not utilize traditional scrolling.

stories.title: BLOND designs modular cloud hardware
stories.summary: Industrial design studio BLOND has created the Edge Node 01 V2, a decentralized cloud hardware unit featuring magnetic swappable panels and a translucent amber shell. The design aims to make distributed infrastructure durable and scalable while allowing it to blend into domestic environments without visible screws.

stories.title: Techmagnate acquires The Minimalist
stories.summary: Digital marketing agency Techmagnate has acquired a majority stake in creative agency The Minimalist. The combined entity will employ approximately 500 people with annual revenue exceeding Rs 100 crore. Both agencies will continue to operate under their existing brand names following the undisclosed financial transaction.

stories.title: Vietnamese cultural identity as creative inspiration
stories.summary: Vietnamese cultural identity is derived from the values and history of 54 ethnic groups. Young artists are increasingly drawing upon these traditional elements and cultural heritage as a reservoir of material for artistic creation and the development of new cultural products.

stories.title: Dungeons & Dragons and World of Warcraft crossover
stories.summary: Dungeons & Dragons and World of Warcraft are collaborating on a gameplay expansion book. This marks the first full-blooded crossover between the two franchises, following a 2003 standalone RPG. Over 50 artists contributed to the project, which blends the two fantasy worlds into a single setting.

stories.title: Adobe discusses AI integration in creative tools
stories.summary: Adobe is integrating AI across its creative suite to improve user efficiency. While online users have threatened to leave the platform over these changes, the company maintains that creativity remains at the forefront of its products. Designers are now being asked to decide what tasks to hand off.

stories.title: Google patent details personalized AI video feeds
stories.summary: Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel, designed to generate video feeds based on user data. The patent describes a future where users are the main character of every story. While the patent was rejected, the company may still appeal or resubmit the proposal.

stories.title: AffCollect updates brand identity
stories.summary: Affiliate management platform AffCollect has rebranded with a new logo and colour palette. The company says the update reflects its focus on simplifying affiliate performance and financial management. The new website aims to provide a clearer overview of the platform and its capabilities for igaming affiliate operations.

AI impact on UX design in 2026
stories.summary: AI has transformed the field of UX design throughout 2026. The shift has introduced unpredictable and significant changes to the industry.

stories.title: Canva adds AI-powered resume builder
stories.summary: Canva has introduced an AI-powered resume builder that suggests layouts and designs for users. The tool allows individuals to input personal information and professional summaries into templates without requiring advanced graphic design skills. It is marketed as a way to create visually appealing resumes for various industries.

stories.title: PixelLoupe offers open-source raw photo editing for Mac
stories.summary: Pixegen has released PixelLoupe, a free, open-source raw photo editor for macOS. The software imports Lightroom Classic catalogs and runs natively on Apple hardware. It is MIT licensed and includes familiar keyboard shortcuts for photographers who prefer to avoid monthly subscription fees for their editing tools.

stories.title: CSS-Tricks previews upcoming scrollytelling article
stories.summary: CSS-Tricks is preparing to publish an art-directed article featuring scroll animations and randomness. The project, created by Lee Meyer, aims to blend 2013-style web aesthetics with 2026 technology. The piece is scheduled for release on December 16.

stories.title: CSS-Tricks covers style queries in course update
stories.summary: CSS-Tricks has released a module on resilient CSS, covering style queries, math functions, and relative colors. The course is currently discounted until December 2, 2026. The material focuses on practical, reusable patterns for developers looking to move beyond traditional modifier classes and attribute selectors.

stories.title: System76 releases Pop!_OS 26.04
stories.summary: System76 has updated its Pop!_OS distribution to version 26.04 LTS. The release includes improvements to the Cosmic desktop environment, aiming to make it more competitive with GNOME. The update introduces several design features intended for power users.

stories.title: GibHub
OpenEight introduces deterministic control for AI agents
stories.summary: OpenEight has launched a control layer designed for AI agents. The company describes the product as a deterministic system for managing agent behavior.

stories.title: Omi launches 2.0 version
stories.summary: Omi has released version 2.0 of its platform. The company claims the software can build any product idea and take it live into production.

stories.title: Statefold debuts autonomous coding agents
stories.summary: Statefold has introduced coding agents designed to operate independently. The company states that these agents continue working even when the user is away from the computer.

stories.title: Sen Việt releases bilingual input method
stories.summary: Sen Việt has launched a bilingual input method compatible with macOS, Windows, and Linux. The tool is designed to support smart text entry for multiple languages.

stories.title: Sawai Man Mahal project details
stories.summary: The Taj Sawai Man Mahal in Jaipur is a hospitality adaptive re-use project designed by Gyanendra Singh Shekhawat of IDEAS. The site covers 37,173.77 square meters and is situated near the 19th-century gardens of the city. Photography for the project was provided by Jaideep Oberoi.

stories.title: Vision Board Studio founder on retail design
stories.summary: Aditi Kotak established Vision Board Studio in 2011 after identifying a need for professional visual merchandising in India. Her approach is informed by early international retail exposure and professional experience with brands including Levi’s and Tanishq. The studio focuses on retail design and customer experience.

stories.title: AD India features November home designs
stories.summary: AD India has highlighted ten homes described as nourishing and enriching for their residents. The selection includes an Art Deco villa belonging to Vikram Goyal. The publication suggests that the beauty of these spaces lies in how they reflect the personalities and aspirations of those living there.

stories.title: Cabinets & me focuses on ergonomic design
stories.summary: Bengaluru-based Cabinets & me manufactures architectural cabinetry including kitchens and wardrobes. Founders Guruswaroop and Charan state their designs pair Scandinavian practicality with Italian color palettes. The company emphasizes ergonomic efficiency and maintains close coordination between its design and manufacturing operations.

stories.title: Lakshmi Venu files family asset partition suit
stories.summary: Lakshmi Venu has filed a suit in the Madras High Court seeking the partition of joint-family assets belonging to the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family. The development is part of a broader roundup of startup and corporate news for November 25, 2026.

stories.title: Assisted banking services reach local populations
stories.summary: The National Payments Corporation of India reported 25.47 billion transactions as of October 2026. Despite the growth of UPI, banks are using the business correspondent model to provide assisted banking services through local access points for populations that still require help with basic financial functions.

stories.title: LocalCircles reports widespread use of dark patterns
stories.summary: A LocalCircles survey indicates that 94 percent of frequently used online platforms in India employ deceptive design practices known as dark patterns. These practices often mislead users into unintended actions like sharing data. Meanwhile, CortexSpark Ventures has launched a 1,000 crore rupee fund for deeptech and AI.

stories.title: ASCI reports high rate of digital ad violations
stories.summary: The Advertising Standards Council of India found that digital platforms accounted for 98 percent of advertising violations between April and September 2026. Meta contributed 73.4 percent of these breaches. Of the advertisements reviewed, 72 percent contained misleading claims. Proactive monitoring identified 85 percent of the violations.

stories.title: V-Guard launches heat management wire campaign
stories.summary: V-Guard Industries has introduced an integrated campaign for its Cool Wires range in Kerala, Karnataka and Odisha. The company states the campaign shifts the focus from fire risks to heat management. The products utilize the ICE 300 Engineering platform for insulation, copper and eco engineering.

stories.title: Leash Biosciences secures 11 million dollars
stories.summary: Leash Biosciences has raised 11 million dollars to expand its automated laboratory and virtual research environments. The company reports its AI agents have completed 100,000 virtual experimental sequences using 44 billion measurements. The funding will support additional biological experiments and new partnerships with pharmaceutical companies.

stories.title: Capable raises 38 million dollars for AI drug discovery
stories.summary: Biotech firm Capable has raised 38 million dollars to automate drug discovery. The company uses AI to design molecules and automated equipment to test them on cells and mice. Its first candidate is a peptide intended to reduce sleep. The firm plans to move assets to pharma companies.

stories.title: Cosine Robots raises 22.36 crore rupees
stories.summary: Bengaluru-based Cosine Robots has raised 22.36 crore rupees led by Avaana Capital. The startup, founded by IIT Patna alumni, plans to use the funds to scale manufacturing of its proprietary integrated servo actuators. The company aims to build affordable humanoids by focusing on robotic joint components.

stories.title: IIT Patna graduates pivot to robotic joints
stories.summary: Two IIT Patna graduates founded Cosine Robots to build affordable humanoids, later focusing on the servo actuators that control robotic movement. The Bengaluru-based startup has raised 22.36 crore rupees to expand its research and production facilities. They previously held roles at Amazon and Google.

stories.title: Aeravti Ventures launches second fund
stories.summary: Aeravti Ventures has launched its second fund with a target of 300 crore rupees, securing over 150 crore rupees at its first close. The firm plans to deploy the capital over ten years into early-stage startups focused on food security, health infrastructure and physical infrastructure.

stories.title: DLI-backed C2i Semiconductors raises $15 million from Peak XV, marking largest funding round for Indian chip startup - D
Cosine Robots raises 2.4 million dollars
stories.summary: Robotics hardware startup Cosine Robots has raised 2.4 million dollars to scale its research and production facility in Bengaluru. Founded in 2024, the company develops integrated servo actuators that convert energy into physical movement. The funding round was led by Avaana Capital with participation from angel investors.

Northwest Missouri State University hosts senior art exhibition
stories.summary: Eleven graduating students are presenting their work at Northwest Missouri State University. Associate professor Sarah Sipling organized the exhibition to showcase the culmination of years of learning and experimentation. The show features pieces from art education and graphic design majors as they prepare to enter professional careers.

stories.title: ‘Drawn by a Fleshy Human’: Rob Manuel on writing 81 jokes on the ZX81 for his new book - Design Week
Beano Brain report identifies Gen Alpha brand preferences
stories.summary: Brands that resonate with Gen Alpha prioritize autonomy, discovery, sharing, and collecting, according to the 2026 Coolest Brands report by Beano Brain. The study suggests that building affinity with children early can lead to long-term consumer relationships that persist through adolescence and into adulthood.

stories.title: Ambarella and Sigma Connectivity partner to speed up edge AI product development - New Electronics
INTOPS to showcase CMF materials at Design Korea 2026
stories.summary: The CMF brand hida, owned by INTOPS, will display over 100 color, material, and finish samples at the Design Korea 2026 fair in Seoul. The event focuses on industry trends including AI transformation and user experience. The exhibition runs through November 29 at the COEX center.

stories.title: Cervus CVT tractor receives German Design Award
stories.summary: The Cervus CVT tractor has won gold in the Excellent Product Design category at the German Design Awards. Developed with CNH Industrial, the tractor previously received Red Dot and BIG SEE awards. It was also named Tractor of the Year 2027 in the HighPower category earlier this month.

stories.title: Madeleine Blanchfield Architects named Interior Designer of the Year
stories.summary: Madeleine Blanchfield Architects received the Interior Designer of the Year title at the 2026 Belle Fanuli Interior Design Awards in Sydney. The event, now in its 16th year, recognizes outstanding work across residential, retail, and commercial sectors. David Hicks was also inducted into the Hall of Fame.

stories.title: RBI clears SBI Mutual Fund to acquire stake in South Indian Bank
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has approved a proposal for SBI Mutual Fund to acquire up to a 9.99 percent stake in South Indian Bank. The acquisition remains subject to regulatory conditions and compliance requirements for the asset management company.

research.title: CHORAL: A Multi-Agent Scaffold for Longitudinal Prognostic Reasoning from Patient-Generated Health Data
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Longitudinal patient-generated health data can inform prognostic reasoning about how patients' conditions may evolve between follow-up visits. Existing approaches summarize trajectories or predict symptom states, but provide limited support for examining how heterogeneous evidence informs prognosis. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

CRAB H extends the ARC governance architecture by introducing the task as a first-class governance object, represented through Task Requirement Profiles TRP. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
